## Overview

ARISTOTLE (ClinicalTrials.gov number NCT00412984) compared [apixaban](./apixaban.md) 5 mg twice daily with [warfarin](./warfarin.md) (target international normalized ratio 2.0 to 3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke, over a median follow-up of 1.8 years. The trial was designed to test noninferiority with key secondary objectives of superiority for the primary outcome, major bleeding and death from any cause ([src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1.md)).

## Reported results

The primary outcome occurred at 1.27% per year with apixaban versus 1.60% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI 0.66 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.01 for superiority). Major bleeding was 2.13% versus 3.09% per year and death from any cause 3.52% versus 3.94% ([src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1.md)).

The trial was funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb and [Pfizer](./pfizer.md) and is one of the four trials pooled in the meta-analysis of new oral anticoagulants ([src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1.md), [src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63](viking://user/ulab0001/resources/p/pmed01/sources/src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63.md)).
